articles.title: 'I am an average student': 19-yr-old ends life over low NEET marks in Maharashtra
articles.description: Tragedy struck in Jalalpur village as a 19-year-old girl reportedly took her own life on Saturday. Authorities discovered a note revealing her distress over disappointing NEET re-examination results, where she scored 166, falling short of the 177 needed. This heartbreaking incident comes just weeks after another NEET-associated death in Nashik. Students are reminded to stay resilient and persevere through academic challenges.

articles.title: Gold, silver price live updates today: Gold prices jump over 1% as easing Middle East tensions drag oil lower, Fed decision in focus
articles.full_text: Gold prices rose more than 1% in early trade as hopes of a de-escalation in tensions between the US and Iran pushed crude oil prices lower, reducing concerns over inflation. Spot gold climbed 1.4% to $4,110.56 an ounce, while US gold futures advanced 1% to $4,112.10. Analysts said the decline in oil prices, coupled with a weaker US dollar, created a favourable environment for the yellow metal. "Gold is a clear beneficiary today of the dual price action in oil and the US dollar, both of which have dropped on de-escalation hopes between the US and Iran. Lower oil is easing inflation concerns," Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade told Reuters. International bullion markets also traded on a stronger footing in the previous week, despite sharp fluctuations driven by geopolitical developments. Comex gold futures for August delivery advanced by $52, or 1.3%, to settle at $4,070.8 an ounce in New York. Silver witnessed even stronger momentum, with the September contract climbing by nearly 5% to $58.90 an ounce. Analysts attributed the recovery to easing crude oil prices after an initial surge triggered by concerns over energy supply disruptions. The rebound suggests that investors continued to seek exposure to precious metals as uncertainty persisted across financial markets. However, experts believe future gains will depend on incoming economic data and signals from major central banks. Beyond monetary policy, developments in the US-Iran conflict continue to shape sentiment in the precious metals market. Analysts say geopolitical uncertainty has kept safe-haven demand intact, even as crude oil prices remain volatile. During last week, Brent crude briefly climbed above the $100-a-barrel mark after Houthi strikes on Saudi-owned vessels raised concerns over possible supply disruptions. However, it cooled 5% as peace signs are beginning to emerge between the nations. Although oil prices have eased, the episode highlighted how quickly geopolitical events can influence inflation expectations and investor behaviour. According to market experts, any escalation in regional tensions or fresh disruptions to global energy supplies could once again boost demand for gold and silver as defensive investment options. The US Federal Reserve's upcoming monetary policy decision is expected to be the biggest driver for gold and silver prices in the coming days. Investors are closely watching not only the interest rate announcement but also the central bank's outlook on inflation and economic growth. Any indication of future rate cuts or a softer policy stance could improve the appeal of non-yielding assets such as gold. On the other hand, a hawkish tone may strengthen the US dollar and Treasury yields, limiting gains in bullion. Market participants will also closely analyse comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh after the policy announcement for clues on the future trajectory of interest rates and what they could mean for precious metal prices.

articles.title: Oil prices fall 5%: Crude cools as US-Iran pause fuels hopes of diplomatic breakthrough
articles.description: Oil prices dropped sharply as the United States and Iran held back from launching fresh strikes. This pause raised hopes that diplomacy could ease Middle East tensions and restore shipping. Brent crude futures fell significantly, trading at their lowest levels in nearly a week. Shipping through key trade routes remained subdued despite the pause in attacks. Uncertainty continues to linger over the conflict and its impact on energy markets.

A total of 6,160 candidates have registered for the admission process so far.
